decisionContext.lockedTarget: A transcendent reality includes an objective morality that guides life and makes virtuous living satisfying.

components.text: There is a transcendent objective morality that guides human life.
Living virtuously under that morality is satisfying even without explicit belief in God.

bundles.sourceExcerpt: >> All that means is that the fall does not explain the proclivity to sin because Eve already had it. It does not explain the existence of evil because knowledge of that already existed before she committed the fall. It also doesn't explain the origin of suffering because of course Eve's punishment for eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

decisionContext.lockedTarget: Eve already possessed moral categories through the image of God, understood the command, and freely disobeyed it, thereby creating the fall's consequences.

components.text: Eve possessed moral categories and could understand God's command before eating from the tree.
She knew she ought not disobey but freely chose to do so.
That act of disobedience produced the fall's consequences.

decisionContext.lockedTarget: On Kanojia's account, an emergency-room duty is only consequential rather than morally or virtuously compelling.

components.text: Kanojia's emergency-room duty is not a moral compulsion in terms of virtue.
It instead identifies a consequence of acting one way rather than another.
